questions.question_text:
A relationship is given by the table below. Is it linear, quadratic or exponential?
$\begin{array}{c|ccccc} x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ y & 7 & 11 & 15 & 19 & 23 \end{array}$

options.why: The $y$-values rise by a constant $+4$, not by a constant ratio, so it is linear not exponential.
The first differences are already constant at $4$; a quadratic needs constant second differences.

questions.solution_text:
The $y$-values go $7,11,15,19,23$, rising by $4$ each time.
A constant first difference means it is a linear relationship.

questions.question_text: A rumour spreads so that the number of people who have heard it triples each hour. Which type of relationship is this?

options.why: Tripling multiplies by a constant ratio; a linear model would add the same number each hour.
There is no squared quantity or turning point; a constant ratio is the exponential pattern.

questions.solution_text:
Tripling every hour multiplies by a constant ratio of $3$.
So it is an exponential relationship.

questions.question_text:
A relationship is given by the table below. It grows fast, so a student guesses exponential. Decide whether it is linear, quadratic or exponential.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ y & 2 & 5 & 10 & 17 \end{array}$

options.why: The ratios $5\div2=2.5$ and $10\div5=2$ are not equal, so there is no constant ratio.
The first differences $3,5,7$ are not constant, so it is not linear.

questions.solution_text:
The ratios $5\div2$ and $10\div5$ are not equal, so it is not exponential.
The first differences are $3,5,7$ and the second differences are both $2$.
A constant second difference means it is a quadratic relationship.
